claim.why_it_matters: The rest of the right column is flattened to one indent level, so sub-entries cannot be told from top-level entries.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of PDF page 869 (printed page 847, Index) shows the right column with two indent levels: top-level entries such as 'IN phrase', 'Incompatibility flagging 49', 'Index', 'INDEXED BY phrase 86, 512, 521', 'Indicators 22', 'INITIAL clause', 'Initial data 115, 238, 386', and indented sub-entries such as 'COPY statement 32', 'With identifiers 87', 'With qualification 85', 'Definition 308', 'CD entry 656', 'OCCURS clause 306', 'Comment 22, 23' ... 'Source 23', 'PROGRAM-ID paragraph 186'. In page-869.md every right-column line from 'COPY statement 32' to 'Initial program 117' carries the same three-space indent and no   marker, while the left column correctly uses   for sub-entries. The text is all present, but the parent/child relation that carries meaning in an index is lost: for example, 'Initial data' and 'Incompatibility flagging' read the same as the sub-entries 'CD entry' and 'PROGRAM-ID paragraph' of INITIAL clause. Both sources are quoted accurately. This is a structural index-hierarchy defect with no normative effect.
